name: Yale Stealth Positioning Lanyard
title: Yale Stealth Positioning Lanyard: Uses & Buying Guide
meta: The Yale Stealth positioning lanyard gives climbers a rope lanyard for work positioning in the canopy and on spars. How it works, setup tips, and what to check.
tagline: A Yale rope positioning lanyard for climbers who want a smooth, adjustable attachment.
summary: The Yale Stealth positioning lanyard is a rope lanyard from Yale Cordage built to hold you in position while you work, whether you are flipping up a spar or tying in a second point in the canopy. Pair it with a mechanical adjuster or friction hitch and a pair of locking carabiners to suit the way you climb.
highlights: Used for work positioning and as a second attachment point
Runs with a friction hitch or mechanical adjuster
Suits removals, spar work, and canopy pruning
Lighter and more adjustable than a steel-core flipline
specs: Friction hitch or mechanical adjuster (check listing)

body.h: How a positioning lanyard earns its keep
p: On a removal the lanyard is what lets you lean back against the stem with both hands free for the saw. In the canopy it doubles as a second attachment while you reposition your main line or reach out to a limb. A rope lanyard like the Yale Stealth gives you a smooth, adjustable hold that you can shorten and lengthen with one hand.

Most climbers run a rope lanyard with a friction hitch or a mechanical adjuster such as a rope grab on one end and a locking carabiner on each end clipped to the saddle side D-rings. Compare other rope lanyards if you want a different length or diameter.

A rope lanyard is not cut-resistant. When you are running a saw near it, keep the bar well clear or switch to a wire-core flipline for heavy spar work. Choose a length that wraps the trunks you usually climb with room to adjust.

Check the rope for cuts, glazing, and stiff or flat spots, and look at the eyes, stitching or splices, and hardware before every climb. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I cut near a rope lanyard?
faq.a: Only with great care. A rope lanyard can be cut by a saw in an instant, so many climbers use a steel-core flipline or a second tie-in when doing heavy cutting on a spar.

faq.q: What else do I need to run this lanyard?
faq.a: Usually two locking carabiners and an adjuster, either a friction hitch or a mechanical rope grab. Check what the listing includes before you order.

name: Husqvarna Air Purge Bulb for T540XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna T540XP Mark II Primer Bulb (Air Purge)
h1: Husqvarna T540XP Mark II Primer Bulb (Air Purge)
meta: Replacement Husqvarna T540XP Mark II primer bulb, also called the air purge bubble. Why it cracks, how it affects starting, and what to check when you swap it.
tagline: Replacement air purge (primer) bulb for the Husqvarna T540XP Mark II top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540XP Mark II primer bulb, often called the air purge bubble, replaces a cracked or soft bulb so the saw primes properly before a cold start. It is a small part, but a split bulb can leave a top-handle saw hard to start or leaking fuel.
highlights: Fits the Husqvarna T540XP Mark II
Fixes fuel weeping from a split bulb
Cheap part worth keeping in the truck

p: The air purge bulb pulls fuel through the carburetor and pushes air out of the system before you start the saw. On a top-handle that rides on a climber's saddle all day, the bulb takes knocks against bark and gets baked in the sun, and fuel slowly hardens the material.

Signs it is time to replace it: the bulb stays flat after you press it, does not fill with fuel, or shows cracks and fuel weeping around the edge. Any of those can leave the saw hard to start right when you are hanging in the tree.
Because the T540XP Mark II is a top-handle saw that often starts in the tree, a dependable prime matters more than usual. A fresh bulb is a two-dollar fix that saves a lot of pulling at height.

Confirm the bulb matches your saw before ordering, since the Mark II and earlier T540XP models are not always interchangeable for every part. Work on a cool saw, drain or close off fuel as needed, and seat the new bulb fully so it seals.

Browse other power equipment parts if you are doing a broader tune-up. Wear chainsaw protection, eye and hearing protection, and follow the operator's manual and ANSI Z133 when running or servicing a saw.

faq.q: Will this bulb fit the original T540XP?
faq.a: It is listed for the T540XP Mark II. Check the part number against your saw's parts list before ordering for an earlier model.

faq.q: Is it safe to run a saw with a cracked primer bulb?
faq.a: No. A cracked bulb can leak fuel onto a hot saw and cause hard starting. Replace it before using the saw again.

name: Teufelberger Tachyon Climbing Rope (Green and Blue)
title: Teufelberger Tachyon Climbing Rope, Green and Blue
h1: Teufelberger Tachyon Climbing Rope, Green and Blue
meta: Teufelberger Tachyon is a light 11.5 mm arborist climbing rope that runs smoothly in hitches and devices. Who it suits, how it handles, and how to care for it.
tagline: A light 11.5 mm arborist climbing rope that handles well for MRS and SRS work.
summary: Teufelberger Tachyon is a light, supple 11.5 mm climbing rope for arborists who want a line that feels easy in the hand and runs cleanly through hitches and mechanical devices. This green and blue colorway makes it easy to pick out from rigging lines on a busy job.
highlights: Light and flexible in the hand
Works for MRS and many SRS setups
Green and blue colorway for quick identification

p: Tachyon is aimed at climbers who want a lighter, more flexible rope than a heavy 1/2 in work line. At 11.5 mm it sits in the sweet spot for most current friction hitches and mechanical devices, and it is easy to haul up through a long canopy.

It suits everyday pruning, spending long days moving through the crown, and removals where you want a rope that does not fight you. Check that your hitch cord and device are rated for an 11.5 mm rope before you climb on it. Compare other 24-strand climbing ropes if you want a firmer or heavier line.
Keep the rope in a bag away from saw fuel, bar oil, and sharp tools, and do not stand on it in the truck. Wash it per the maker's instructions when it gets loaded with sap and grit.

Inspect the cover and feel the core along its full length before each climb for cuts, glazing, flat spots, and stiffness. Retire it if you find damage. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Is Tachyon good for SRS?
faq.a: Many climbers use 11.5 mm ropes on SRS, but check that your specific device is rated for this rope before use.

faq.q: What length should I buy?
faq.a: Pick a length that is at least twice the height of the tallest tie-in you expect for MRS. For SRS you need roughly the height of your anchor plus extra for basal setups.

name: 5/8 in x 30 ft Standard Crane Sling
title: 5/8 x 30 ft Standard Crane Sling for Tree Removal
h1: 5/8 in x 30 ft Standard Crane Sling
meta: A 5/8 x 30 ft standard crane sling for choking picks on crane-assisted tree removals. How it is used, how to size it, and what to inspect before each pick.
tagline: A 30 ft rope crane sling for choking large picks on crane-assisted removals.
summary: This 5/8 in x 30 ft standard crane sling gives you the reach to choke large-diameter trunks and wide tops on crane-assisted tree removals. The standard version is a practical choice for crews that run crane jobs regularly and want a sling they can replace without worry.
highlights: 30 ft length for large trunks and wide tops
Rope construction is easy to choke and handle
Check the tag for rated capacity

body.h: Using a crane sling on removals
p: On a crane job the climber sets the sling around the piece, the operator takes tension, and the cut is made only once the crane has the weight. A 30 ft sling gives you enough length to choke big trunk sections and spread-out tops, or to double-wrap a smaller piece for a better bite.
Choke high enough above the cut that the piece hangs balanced, and keep the sling clear of the kerf. Compare other crane slings if you need a shorter or heavier option.
Standard and premium slings differ mainly in rope and construction, so read the tag on the sling you receive rather than assuming a capacity.

Before each pick, look over the full length for cuts, chafed or melted fibers, and stiff spots, and check the eyes and splices. Retire the sling if you find damage or if the tag is missing or unreadable.

Know the weight of the piece and the rated capacity for the hitch you are using; a choker hitch reduces capacity. Rig only within the rated strength of every component, inspect gear before each job, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions. Crane work also requires a qualified operator and a pre-lift plan.

faq.q: What is the difference between standard and premium crane slings?
faq.a: They generally differ in rope type and construction. Check the tag and listing for the rated capacities of the version you buy.

faq.q: Can I use a crane sling for regular rigging with a lowering line?
faq.a: It can serve as a choker, but always confirm the sling's rated capacity for the dynamic loads involved in rigging.

name: Courant Cross Pro XL Gear Bag
title: Courant Cross Pro XL Gear Bag for Arborists
h1: Courant Cross Pro XL Gear Bag
meta: The Courant Cross Pro XL is a large gear bag for carrying a saddle, rope, and hardware to the job. What fits, how it carries, and how it keeps a kit organized.
tagline: A large Courant gear bag for hauling a full climbing kit to and from the job.
summary: The Courant Cross Pro XL is a big gear bag for climbers who want a saddle, rope, and hardware in one place on the way to the job. The XL size gives room for a full kit, so you are not digging through the truck for a missing carabiner at the base of the tree.
highlights: Extra-large version of the Cross Pro bag
Room for a saddle, rope, and hardware
Keeps life-support gear away from fuel and tools
Carries to the base of the tree

body.h: Why a dedicated gear bag matters
p: Climbing gear lives a hard life in the back of a truck, next to saws, fuel, and chipper parts. A dedicated bag keeps your saddle, ropes, and hardware away from bar oil and sharp edges and keeps everything together so you can set up quickly at the tree.

The XL version is aimed at climbers who carry a lot: a saddle, a climbing line, a lanyard, a few hitch cords, and a handful of carabiners and pulleys. Compare other gear bags if you want something smaller for a day kit.

A bag with a wide opening also makes it easier to see what is inside before you leave the shop, so a missing hitch cord or pulley gets noticed in the yard instead of at the top of the driveway. Clip-in points and a stiff base help it stand open on uneven ground.
Pack heavy items low and keep sharp hardware away from rope. Let wet gear dry out of the bag before storing it, since damp, closed bags speed up mildew and wear on textiles.

A good bag protects your gear, but it does not replace inspection. Check every piece of life-support equipment before each climb. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Will a saddle and a rope fit in the XL?
faq.a: It is sized for a full kit, but exact capacity depends on the saddle and rope length. Check the listed dimensions against your gear.

faq.q: How do I clean the bag?
faq.a: Brush out debris, wash with mild soap and water, and air dry. Avoid solvents that can damage the fabric.

name: Air Filter for Husqvarna 572XP
title: Husqvarna 572XP Air Filter: Replacement Guide
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 572XP air filter to keep dust and chips out of the engine. When to clean or swap the filter and why it matters for power and engine life.
tagline: A replacement air filter for the Husqvarna 572XP professional chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 572XP air filter replaces a worn or torn filter so the saw breathes clean air and holds its power through a long day of bucking and felling. A clogged filter costs you power and fuel, and a damaged one lets fine dust into the engine.
highlights: Keeps chips and dust out of the engine
Helps the saw hold power and run clean
Worth having a spare in the truck

p: A 572XP pulls a lot of air when it is buried in a big log, and that air is full of fine chips and dust. The filter is the only thing between that debris and the engine. A clogged filter makes the saw run rich and lose power; a torn one lets grit through to the cylinder and piston.
Swapping in a fresh filter is one of the cheapest ways to protect an expensive saw. Browse other power equipment parts if you are doing a full service.

The 572XP is often run with a long bar in big wood, which means long cuts at high load and a lot of fine sawdust around the intake. That makes a clean filter even more important on this saw than on a small limbing saw.

Check the filter at the end of each day and more often in dry, dusty conditions or when cutting dead wood. Clean it per the operator's manual, and replace it if it is torn, deformed, or will not come clean.

Make sure the filter seats fully so nothing bypasses it, and keep the area around the filter cover clean when you open it. Wear chainsaw protection, eye and hearing protection, and follow the operator's manual and ANSI Z133 when running or servicing a saw.

faq.q: How often should I replace the air filter?
faq.a: There is no fixed interval. Clean it regularly and replace it when it is damaged or no longer comes clean.

faq.q: Will this filter fit other Husqvarna saws?
faq.a: It is listed for the 572XP. Check your saw's parts list before using it on another model.

name: Husqvarna X-COM Active Headband Communication System
title: Husqvarna X-COM Active Headband Communication Set
h1: Husqvarna X-COM Active Headband Communication System
meta: Husqvarna X-COM Active is a headband hearing protector with built-in crew communication, so climbers and ground crews can talk clearly while saws are running.
tagline: Hearing protection with built-in crew communication for climbers and ground workers.
summary: The Husqvarna X-COM Active is a headband-style hearing protector with a built-in communication system, so a climber and the ground crew can talk while saws and chippers are running. Clear communication cuts down on hand signals and shouting during rigging and felling.
highlights: Lets climbers and ground crew talk over saw noise
Useful for rigging, felling, and crane work

p: On a rigging job, the climber and the person on the lowering line need to be in sync. Hand signals work until a limb blocks the view, and shouting does not work at all with a saw running. A communication headset lets the climber call for slack, tension, or a stop clearly, which makes rigging safer and faster.
The X-COM Active combines that communication with hearing protection in one headband unit. Compare other communication systems if you need a helmet-mounted setup instead.

On crane jobs, headset comms between the climber, ground crew, and operator are often the difference between a smooth pick and a near miss. Even on everyday pruning, being able to say exactly which limb is coming down next keeps the drop zone clear and the crew working in step.

A headband model suits ground workers and anyone who does not wear a helmet with integrated muffs. Check that the cups seal fully around your ears; glasses arms and hair can break the seal and reduce protection.

Agree on standard calls before the job starts and confirm the system works before anyone leaves the ground. Communication gear supports, but does not replace, a clear work plan and trained crew. Follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions.

faq.q: Can I use the X-COM Active with a helmet?
faq.a: This is the headband version. If you want communication on a helmet, look for a helmet-mounted model that fits your helmet.

faq.q: Does it still protect my hearing when the radio is on?
faq.a: It is designed as a hearing protector first. Check the stated noise reduction and fit it properly so it seals.

name: Preformed Line Products Wedge Grips
title: Preformed Line Products Wedge Grips for Tree Cabling
meta: Preformed Line Products wedge grips terminate steel strand in tree cabling systems. How they work, sizing to the strand, and installation and inspection tips.
tagline: Wedge-style dead-end grips for terminating steel strand in tree cabling systems.
summary: Preformed Line Products wedge grips are dead-end grips used to terminate steel strand when installing static cabling in trees. They grab the strand as load comes on, giving a quick, consistent termination that pairs with eye bolts or lag hooks.
highlights: Dead-end grip for steel cabling strand
Pairs with thimbles and eye hardware
Must be sized to the strand diameter

body.h: How wedge grips work in cabling
p: In a static cabling system, steel strand runs between anchors in two leaders to limit how far they can move apart. Each end of the strand needs a termination. A wedge grip does this by clamping the strand inside a tapered body, so the harder the strand pulls, the tighter the grip holds.
Compared with hand-wrapped dead ends or clamps, a wedge grip is quick to install and gives a consistent result from tree to tree. Compare other cabling hardware for eye bolts, thimbles, and strand.

Wedge grips are common in static steel cabling, where the strand runs between eye bolts or lag hooks set in each leader. Because the grip is quick to install, it saves time when you are working off a lanyard high in the crown, but the job still needs the same care in anchor placement, strand tension, and hardware selection as any cabling install.

Match the grip to the exact strand size you are installing, and follow ANSI A300 cabling standards and the manufacturer's installation steps. Use a thimble where the grip bears on an eye to protect the hardware.
Inspect cabling systems on a regular schedule for wear, corrosion, and changes in the tree. Cabling should be designed and installed by a qualified arborist.

faq.q: Can one wedge grip size fit any strand?
faq.a: No. Each grip is made for a specific strand diameter. Use the size that matches the strand you are installing.

faq.q: Do I need a thimble with a wedge grip?
faq.a: Follow the manufacturer's instructions for the system you are using. A thimble is often used where the termination wraps an eye.

name: DMM Perfect O Carabiner
title: DMM Perfect O Carabiner: Oval Auto-Locking Connector
meta: The DMM Perfect O is a symmetrical oval carabiner that keeps pulleys, ascenders, and rope grabs sitting square. Where it fits in a kit and how to inspect it.
tagline: A symmetrical oval carabiner that keeps pulleys and devices sitting square.
summary: The DMM Perfect O is a symmetrical oval carabiner, and that shape keeps pulleys, rope grabs, and ascenders centered instead of sliding toward the spine. Arborists use it wherever a device needs to sit square, such as on a hitch-tending pulley or a lanyard adjuster.
highlights: Good partner for pulleys and rope grabs

p: Most carabiners are D or pear shaped, which pulls the load toward the spine. That is fine for a rope, but a pulley or rope grab on a D carabiner can cock sideways. The Perfect O's symmetrical oval lets the device hang centered, so it runs smoothly and loads evenly.

That makes it a natural fit for pulleys below a friction hitch, for rope grabs on a lanyard, and for racking several pieces together. Compare other auto-locking carabiners if you need a larger pear shape for hitches.

An oval carries less load on the major axis than a comparable D because the load is centered rather than near the spine. Check the strength markings on the gate and match the carabiner to the job; do not cross-load it or load it over an edge.

Inspect the gate, locking sleeve, and nose before every climb and retire any carabiner that has been dropped onto a hard surface from height, shows cracks or deep wear, or does not close and lock cleanly. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Is an oval carabiner as strong as a D?
faq.a: Usually a little less on the major axis, because the load sits further from the spine. Check the markings on the specific carabiner.

faq.q: What is the Perfect O best for?
faq.a: Holding pulleys, rope grabs, and ascenders square. It is less suited to holding a bulky friction hitch than a large pear-shaped carabiner.

name: Best Practices for Rigging, 3rd Edition
title: Best Practices for Rigging, 3rd Edition (Book)
meta: Best Practices for Rigging, 3rd edition, is a tree rigging reference for crews and trainees. Who it is for and how to use it with hands-on training.
tagline: A rigging reference for tree crews, trainees, and the people who train them.
summary: Best Practices for Rigging, 3rd edition, is a reference book on tree rigging for arborists, crew leaders, and trainees. It pairs well with hands-on training and gives crews a shared vocabulary for setting rigging points, controlling loads, and choosing gear.
highlights: Third edition of a tree rigging reference
Useful for crew leaders and trainees
Gives crews a shared vocabulary for rigging
Good addition to a shop training library

p: Rigging is where small mistakes turn into big ones: a poorly chosen rigging point, an undersized sling, or a load that runs harder than expected. A good reference book helps crews understand the forces involved and talk through a plan with the same terms.

This edition suits new ground workers learning to run a lowering line, climbers moving into removal work, and crew leaders who run tailgate training. Browse other books and training materials to build out a shop library.

Many crews keep a copy in the truck or the shop so they can review a technique before a tricky removal or answer a question that comes up during a tailgate meeting. It also helps newer workers understand why the crew sets rigging points and lowering devices the way it does, rather than just copying the motions. Pair it with other training materials and certification study guides to build a well-rounded library for the whole crew.

Reading is a starting point, not a substitute for supervised practice. Use the book to prepare for training sessions, review concepts with your crew, and settle questions when someone is unsure about a technique.
Rigging should always be planned and carried out by trained people following ANSI Z133, the current industry practices, and each manufacturer's instructions for the gear in use.

faq.q: Is the 3rd edition the current one?
faq.a: Check the listing for the edition being sold. Newer printings can add updated techniques and gear.

faq.q: Can I learn rigging from a book alone?
faq.a: No. Use it with hands-on training from qualified people, and practice under supervision before rigging on your own.

name: Yale R.I.N.G. Lanyard Kit with DMM Carabiners
title: Yale R.I.N.G. Lanyard Kit with DMM Carabiners
h1: Yale R.I.N.G. Lanyard Kit with DMM Carabiners
meta: A Yale R.I.N.G. lanyard kit with DMM carabiners: a ready-to-climb rope positioning lanyard. What is included, how it sets up, and how to inspect it before use.
tagline: A rope positioning lanyard kit built with Yale rope and DMM carabiners.
summary: This Yale R.I.N.G. lanyard kit with DMM carabiners gives you a ready-to-climb rope positioning lanyard built from Yale rope with DMM connectors. It is a straightforward way to get a matched lanyard setup without sourcing each piece yourself.
highlights: Ready to clip into your saddle
Good for removals and canopy work

body.h: What a lanyard kit saves you
p: Building a lanyard from scratch means matching rope diameter to an adjuster, choosing carabiners that sit right, and making sure everything is compatible. A kit takes care of that, so you can unpack it, check it over, and clip it to your saddle.
The positioning lanyard is the tool that lets you lean back on a spar or hold your place in the canopy with your hands free. Compare other lanyard kits if you want a different length or adjuster.

Kits like this were popular with large tree care companies because every climber gets the same setup, which makes training and inspection simpler. If you are building a kit for a new climber, it removes a lot of guesswork about what fits together.
Clip each end to your saddle's side D-rings with the gates facing away from the tree and the locks engaged. Adjust the length so you can work comfortably without leaning out of balance.

A rope lanyard is not cut-resistant, so keep the saw well clear of it. Inspect the rope, the eyes, and every carabiner before each climb. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Does the kit include an adjuster?
faq.a: Kit contents vary. Check the listing for whether a mechanical adjuster or hitch cord is included.

faq.q: Can I swap the carabiners for my own?
faq.a: Yes, as long as your carabiners are rated for life support, compatible with the eyes, and you follow the maker's instructions.

name: Arborwear After Hours Belt (Chain Design)
title: Arborwear After Hours Belt, Chain Design
h1: Arborwear After Hours Belt, Chain Design
meta: The Arborwear After Hours belt with a chain design is a work belt from a brand built around tree work. How it pairs with work pants and how to fit it.
tagline: An Arborwear work belt with a chain design, made to pair with tree work pants.
summary: The Arborwear After Hours belt in the chain design is a work belt from a brand that makes clothing for tree work. It pairs with climbing and work pants and brings a bit of the trade to your everyday kit.
highlights: Pairs with Arborwear and other work pants
Suits work days and off the job
From an apparel brand built for tree crews

p: A belt has a hard job on a tree crew: you bend, climb, crawl through brush, and haul limbs to the chipper all day. A solid work belt keeps your pants in place without digging in when you squat or kneel.
The chain design gives the After Hours belt a look that nods to the trade, so it works on the job and after it. Pair it with tree climbing pants for a complete work outfit.

Arborwear started with clothing made for climbing and tree work, so its gear tends to be built to take the bending, reaching, and brush that come with the job. The After Hours belt carries that into an accessory you can wear every day, on site or off.

body.h: Fit and wear with a saddle
p: If you wear a climbing saddle, check that the buckle does not sit under the saddle's waist belt where it can press into you on a long climb. Many climbers wear a low-profile belt or none at all in the tree.
Order by your pant waist size and check the listing for sizing guidance. A belt is clothing, not safety gear; never use it as part of a climbing or fall-protection system.

faq.q: How should I size the belt?
faq.a: Most belts are sized by pant waist size. Check the listing's size chart before ordering.

faq.q: Can I wear it under my climbing saddle?
faq.a: Some climbers do, but make sure the buckle does not create a pressure point under the saddle on long climbs.

name: Klein Replacement Barrel Sleeves and Bolts
keyword: klein climber barrel sleeves and bolts
title: Klein Climber Barrel Sleeves and Bolts (Replacement)
h1: Klein Climber Barrel Sleeves and Bolts (Replacement)
meta: Klein climber barrel sleeves and bolts replace worn or lost fasteners on your Klein climbers. When to replace them and how to keep your spurs in safe shape.
tagline: Replacement barrel sleeves and bolts for Klein climbers.
summary: These Klein climber barrel sleeves and bolts replace the fasteners on Klein climbers when they are worn, stripped, or lost. Keeping the hardware tight and in good condition is part of keeping a set of spurs safe to climb on.
highlights: Replaces worn, stripped, or lost hardware
Inexpensive spare to keep in the kit
Helps keep spurs in safe working order

p: Climbing spurs take a beating with every step, and the fasteners on them loosen, wear, or get lost over time. A loose or damaged fastener can let parts shift when you are weighting the spur on a removal.
Barrel sleeves and bolts are a cheap fix that keeps a good set of climbers in service. Browse other replacement gaffs and parts for gaffs, straps, and pads.

Many experienced climbers keep a small bag of spare spur hardware in the truck, since a single missing bolt can sideline a set of climbers in the middle of a job. Checking and replacing these parts is also a good moment to look at the gaffs for sharpness and correct profile.
Use parts made for your specific Klein climber model, tighten them as the manufacturer directs, and check them again after the first climb. Do not substitute generic hardware.

Before every climb, check the shanks, gaffs, straps, and fasteners for cracks, bends, wear, and looseness. Spurs are for removals and emergency access only, never for pruning live trees. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Will these fit any brand of climber?
faq.a: No. They are made for Klein climbers. Check the fit for your specific model before ordering.

faq.q: How often should I check the bolts?
faq.a: Check them before each climb and retighten or replace them as needed.

name: ISC Large Rigging Pulley (Yellow with Green Wheel)
title: ISC Large Rigging Pulley, Yellow with Green Wheel
h1: ISC Large Rigging Pulley, Yellow with Green Wheel
meta: The ISC large rigging pulley redirects lowering lines on tree removals and heavy pruning. How it fits a rigging system, rope sizing, and what to inspect.
tagline: A large ISC rigging pulley for redirecting lowering lines on removals.
summary: The ISC large rigging pulley is a block for redirecting a lowering line on removals and heavy pruning cuts, with yellow side plates and a green sheave that are easy to spot in the canopy. It hangs from a sling at the rigging point and lets the rope run with less friction and wear than a natural crotch.
highlights: Redirects the lowering line at the rigging point
Reduces rope wear compared with a natural crotch
Hangs from a sling or ring

p: On a removal, the rigging point carries the biggest loads in the whole system. Hanging a pulley from a sling there lets the lowering line run smoothly, reduces wear on the rope and the tree, and makes it easier for the ground crew to control the piece with a lowering device.
The bright yellow and green finish helps the climber and ground crew see the block at a glance. Compare other rigging blocks if you need a different rope size or rating.

Large rigging pulleys are usually paired with an eye-to-eye or ring sling sized for the stem at the rigging point. Keep the pulley high enough that the lowering line runs cleanly without rubbing on branches below it.

Match the pulley to the rope diameter you rig with and to the rated strength of the sling and lowering device. Check the markings on the pulley for its working load and minimum breaking strength before use.

Inspect the side plates, axle, and sheave for cracks, grooves, and wobble, and make sure the sheave spins freely. Rig only within the rated strength of every component, inspect gear before each job, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: What rope size does it take?
faq.a: Check the markings and listing for the maximum rope diameter. Running rope larger than rated causes wear and can damage the pulley.

faq.q: Can I use this pulley for climbing?
faq.a: A rigging pulley is designed for rigging loads. Use only devices rated for life support in a climbing system.

name: Honey Badger Tree Climbing Spikes
title: Honey Badger Tree Climbing Spikes (Aluminum Spurs)
meta: Honey Badger tree climbing spikes are aluminum spurs for removal climbers. How lighter spurs feel on long climbs, fit tips, and pre-climb checks.
tagline: Aluminum tree climbing spikes for climbers who spend long days on removals.
summary: Honey Badger tree climbing spikes are aluminum spurs built for climbers who want a lighter set on their feet during long removal days. Less weight at the ankle means less fatigue over a long climb, especially on tall spars.
highlights: Lighter on the leg than steel spurs
Pair with pads and straps sized to you
Gaffs must be kept sharp and in good shape

p: Every step on spurs means lifting that weight with your legs. On a long removal or several in a day, a lighter set of aluminum climbing spikes cuts down on fatigue in your knees and hips compared with heavier steel climbers.
Fit matters as much as weight: the shank should match your lower leg length and the pads should spread the load. Compare other aluminum spurs to find the right length and pad system.

Aluminum spurs are a popular upgrade for climbers who do a lot of removal work, but they still need the same fit and care as any set of climbers. Pads that spread the load and straps that hold the shank snug to your leg make a bigger difference to comfort than weight alone.

Use climbing spurs only for removals and for emergency access, never for pruning a tree that will stay, since gaffs wound the tree. Keep the gaffs sharp and at the correct profile so they bite cleanly instead of cutting out.

Before each climb, check shanks, gaffs, straps, and fasteners for cracks, wear, and looseness, and always climb with a lanyard and climbing line in place. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I prune with climbing spikes?
faq.a: No. Spurs wound the tree. Use them only for removals and emergency access.

faq.q: How do I choose the shank length?
faq.a: Measure from the arch of your foot to just below the knee and match the shank length to that measurement as the maker directs.

name: Arborist Safety Helmets
title: Arborist Safety Helmets for Climbing and Ground Work
meta: Arborist safety helmets for climbers and ground crews: choosing between Type I and Type II, vented and unvented shells, and add-ons like visors and ear muffs.
tagline: Helmets for climbers and ground workers, with the fit and features tree work demands.
summary: Arborist safety helmets protect climbers and ground crews from falling wood, impacts, and the knocks that come with working in and under trees. The right helmet depends on whether you climb, work on the ground, or work near energized lines.
highlights: Options for Type I and Type II impact protection
Mounts for visors, ear muffs, and lights
specs: Mesh visor, ear muffs, headlamp clips

p: Tree work exposes you to impacts from above and from the side. A Type I helmet is tested for impacts to the top of the head, while a Type II helmet is also tested for side impacts, which matter when you can swing into a stem. Climbers need a secure chin strap so the helmet stays on in a fall.
If you work near power lines, choose a helmet with an appropriate electrical rating; vented shells are not rated for electrical work. Browse other safety gear to complete your kit.

Ground workers face many of the same hazards as climbers, from falling deadwood to swinging limbs on a rigging job, so everyone on the site should wear a helmet. A climbing-style helmet with a secure chin strap stays put when you look up, bend over, or work on a slope, which a loose hard hat will not do.
Most climbing-style helmets take a mesh or clear visor, ear muffs, and a headlamp. Make sure accessories are made for your helmet model so they do not compromise the shell.

Adjust the fit so the helmet sits level and does not move when you shake your head. Replace it after any significant impact, and follow the manufacturer's service life guidance. Choose helmets that meet the applicable standard and follow ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Do climbers need a Type II helmet?
faq.a: Many arborists choose Type II for the added side-impact protection. Check your employer's requirements and the standards that apply to your work.

faq.q: Can I use a vented helmet near power lines?
faq.a: No. Vented helmets are not electrically rated. Use a helmet with the right electrical class for line-clearance work.

name: Husqvarna 522iHD60 Battery Hedge Trimmer
title: Husqvarna 522iHD60 Battery Hedge Trimmer Guide
meta: The Husqvarna 522iHD60 is a professional battery hedge trimmer with a 24 in double-sided blade. Who it suits, what it cuts, and battery tips for long days.
tagline: A professional battery hedge trimmer with a long double-sided blade.
summary: The Husqvarna 522iHD60 is a professional battery hedge trimmer with a 60 cm (about 24 in) double-sided blade for shaping hedges and clearing shrubs without gas, fumes, or a pull cord. It runs on Husqvarna's 36V battery system, so it shares packs with other tools in that lineup.
highlights: No fuel mixing, no fumes, quieter than gas
Good for shaping and maintenance trimming

body.h: Where it fits on a tree and landscape crew
p: Hedge work is a big part of many tree and landscape businesses, and a battery trimmer makes it quieter and simpler. The 522iHD60's long double-sided blade covers wide hedges in fewer passes and lets you cut in either direction.
Running on a battery means no fuel to mix and less noise in residential neighborhoods and around clients. Compare other battery-powered equipment if you want tools that share the same batteries.

Battery hedge trimmers also make sense for crews that work early in the morning, near schools or hospitals, or for clients who ask for quieter equipment. A tree crew that also handles hedge and shrub work can cover that side of the business without hauling a separate fleet of gas trimmers. The long blade gives good reach along tall or wide hedges, though a shorter trimmer is easier to control on detailed shaping.

Plan battery capacity around your workload; long hedge days usually call for spare packs or a backpack battery. Keep the blades clean and lubricated, and check them for damage after hitting wire or stone.
Wear eye protection, hearing protection, and gloves, keep both hands on the handles, and remove the battery before clearing jams or cleaning the blade. Follow the operator's manual.

faq.q: Does the 522iHD60 come with a battery?
faq.a: It is often sold as a bare tool. Check the listing for whether a battery and charger are included.

faq.q: What does HD60 mean?
faq.a: It refers to the double-sided hedge trimmer with a 60 cm blade.

name: Husqvarna 10 in Bar, 40 DL, for Battery Pole Saws
title: Husqvarna 10 in Pole Saw Bar, 40 DL (Battery)
h1: Husqvarna 10 in Pole Saw Bar, 40 Drive Links
meta: A Husqvarna 10 in pole saw bar with 40 drive links for Husqvarna battery-powered pole saws. How to match bar and chain, when to replace it, and bar care tips.
tagline: A 10 in replacement bar for Husqvarna battery-powered pole saws.
summary: This Husqvarna 10 in pole saw bar takes a 40 drive link chain and is listed for Husqvarna battery-powered pole saws. Swap it in when the rails are worn, spread, or bent so your pole saw cuts straight again.
highlights: Pair with the matching 3/8 in low-profile chain

body.h: When to replace a pole saw bar
p: Pole saw bars take abuse from reaching into tight crotches and getting pinched in hangers. Worn or spread rails let the chain lean, which makes the saw cut crooked and wear unevenly. A bent bar or a damaged nose sprocket is another reason to swap it.
A fresh bar plus a fresh chain brings a tired pole saw back to clean, straight cuts. Browse other chainsaw bars for different lengths.

Battery pole saws are a favorite for pruning from the ground, raising canopies over driveways, and clearing small limbs without a ladder. A fresh bar keeps the cut straight, which matters a lot when you are cutting at arm's length overhead and need the piece to drop exactly where you planned.
Bar length, pitch, gauge, and drive link count all have to match. This bar takes a 40 drive link chain; confirm pitch and gauge against your saw's manual and the chain you plan to run.

Flip the bar regularly, keep the groove and oil hole clean, and dress burrs from the rails. Remove the battery before handling the bar or chain. Wear chainsaw protection, eye and hearing protection, and follow the operator's manual and ANSI Z133 when running or servicing a saw.

faq.q: Which chain goes on this bar?
faq.a: A 40 drive link chain of the pitch and gauge the bar is made for. The matching Husqvarna 3/8 in low-profile .050 in chain is the common pairing.

faq.q: Will it fit my gas pole saw?
faq.a: It is listed for Husqvarna battery pole saws. Check your saw's mount and manual before using it on another model.

name: Husqvarna 300mm Curved Hand Saw with Scabbard
title: Husqvarna 300mm Curved Hand Saw with Scabbard
h1: Husqvarna 300mm Curved Hand Saw with Scabbard
meta: The Husqvarna 300mm curved hand saw comes with a scabbard for your saddle or belt. How climbers use it for pruning cuts, plus blade care and safe carry tips.
tagline: A 300mm curved pruning saw with scabbard for climbers and ground pruners.
summary: The Husqvarna 300mm curved hand saw has a pull-stroke blade about 12 in long and comes with a scabbard, so it rides on your saddle or belt and is ready for pruning cuts. The curve helps the saw bite on overhead and reaching cuts in the canopy.
highlights: Good for pruning in the canopy and from the ground
Lighter and quieter than a top-handle saw

body.h: Why climbers carry a curved hand saw
p: A hand saw is the go-to for small and medium pruning cuts: it is quiet, precise, and lets you make clean cuts at the branch collar without starting a saw. The curved blade pulls itself into the wood on overhead and reaching cuts, which helps when you are stretched out on a limb.
A 300mm blade is a good all-round length for a saddle saw. Compare other hand saws and scabbards if you want a longer or straight blade.
Many climbers carry both a hand saw and a top-handle saw, using the hand saw for finish cuts and any branch small enough to cut quickly by hand.

Keep the saw in its scabbard whenever you are not cutting, and clip the scabbard where you can reach it without crossing your climbing line or lanyard. Let the teeth do the work on the pull stroke rather than forcing the push.

Wipe sap off the blade after use and replace the blade when the teeth dull or a tooth breaks. Hand saw teeth are very sharp; wear gloves and keep your free hand clear of the cut. Follow ANSI A300 pruning practice and ANSI Z133 safety rules.

faq.q: Can I replace the blade?
faq.a: Check the listing for replacement blade availability for this model.

faq.q: Is 300mm long enough for climbing?
faq.a: It is a common saddle saw length that handles most pruning cuts. Many climbers add a longer saw for larger limbs.

name: Husqvarna 3/8 Micro x .050 40DL Chain for Battery Pole Saws
title: Husqvarna Pole Saw Chain, 3/8 x .050, 40 DL
h1: Husqvarna Pole Saw Chain, 3/8 x .050, 40 DL
meta: Husqvarna pole saw chain, 3/8 low-profile x .050 with 40 drive links, for battery pole saws. How to match it to your bar, sharpen it, and when to replace it.
tagline: A 40 drive link replacement chain for Husqvarna battery pole saws with a 10 in bar.
summary: This Husqvarna pole saw chain is a 3/8 in low-profile, .050 in gauge chain with 40 drive links, listed for Husqvarna battery-powered pole saws. It matches the 10 in pole saw bar, so a fresh chain gets your pole saw cutting fast and straight again.
highlights: Matches the 10 in pole saw bar
specs: Husqvarna battery pole saws with a 10 in bar (check model)

body.h: Matching the chain to your pole saw
p: A chain has to match the bar and sprocket in three ways: pitch, gauge, and drive link count. This chain is 3/8 in low-profile, .050 in gauge, with 40 drive links, which pairs with Husqvarna's 10 in battery pole saw bar.
Keep a spare chain on the truck so a dull or damaged chain does not stop the job. Browse other chainsaw chains for different saws.

Battery pole saws run a narrow kerf chain to get the most cutting out of each charge. That makes sharpness especially important: a dull chain drains the battery faster and leaves rough cuts on the limbs you are pruning.
Sharpen with the file size listed for this chain and keep the depth gauges set correctly. A pole saw chain dulls fast if it touches dirt or a fence wire, so file it as soon as cutting slows down.

Replace the chain when the cutters are filed back to the wear marks, links are cracked, or the chain will not tension properly. Remove the battery before handling the chain. Wear chainsaw protection, eye and hearing protection, and follow the operator's manual and ANSI Z133 when running or servicing a saw.

faq.q: Will this chain fit my gas pole saw?
faq.a: Only if your bar is made for 3/8 in low-profile, .050 in gauge, 40 drive link chain. Check the bar markings.

faq.q: What file size do I need?
faq.a: Use the file size the chain manufacturer lists for this chain; it is usually printed on the packaging.

name: Air Filter for Husqvarna 372XP
title: Husqvarna 372XP Air Filter: Replacement Guide
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 372XP air filter to keep fine dust and chips out of the engine. When to clean or replace it and why it matters for power.
tagline: A replacement air filter for the Husqvarna 372XP chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP air filter replaces a torn, clogged, or worn filter on one of the most popular professional saws ever made. A clean filter keeps the 372XP pulling hard in big wood and protects the engine from fine dust.
highlights: Protects the engine from dust and chips

p: Plenty of 372XPs are still running on tree crews years after they were bought, and a good part of that comes down to basic maintenance. The air filter is first in line: when it clogs, the saw runs rich, loses power, and gets harder to start. When it tears, dust gets into the cylinder and wears the engine.
A replacement filter is cheap insurance on a saw you rely on. Browse other power equipment parts for a full tune-up.

The 372XP is a 70 cc class saw that spends a lot of its life bucking and felling in dusty conditions. Keeping a spare filter in the saw kit means you can swap a dirty one on site and clean it properly back at the shop.
Check and clean the filter daily, and more often when cutting dry or dead wood. Replace it when it is torn, warped, or no longer cleans up, and confirm it seats fully in the housing.

Brush debris away from the cover before opening it so nothing falls into the intake. Wear chainsaw protection, eye and hearing protection, and follow the operator's manual and ANSI Z133 when running or servicing a saw.

faq.q: Does this filter fit the 365 or 371?
faq.a: It is listed for the 372XP. Many saws in that family share parts, but check the part number against your saw's parts list.

faq.q: My saw has lost power. Is the filter the cause?
faq.a: A clogged filter is a common cause. Check it first, then look at the spark plug, fuel, and spark arrestor screen.

name: Husqvarna Battery-Powered Ascender (Tool Only)
title: Husqvarna Battery-Powered Ascender (Tool Only)
h1: Husqvarna Battery-Powered Ascender, Without Battery or Charger
meta: The Husqvarna battery-powered ascender lifts a climber up a fixed rope with a motor instead of leg power. How it works, what it changes, and what to know first.
tagline: A motorized rope ascender for arborists, sold without a battery or charger.
summary: The Husqvarna battery-powered ascender is a motorized device that pulls a climber up a fixed rope, taking much of the effort out of long SRS ascents. This listing is the tool only, without a battery or charger, for crews already running compatible Husqvarna batteries.
highlights: Cuts fatigue on long SRS ascents
Requires training and a backup system
specs: Tool only, no battery or charger

p: Long ascents on a fixed line wear you down before you even make a cut. A powered ascender does the climbing for you: you set your SRS line, attach the device, and it pulls you up the rope while your legs and arms stay fresh for the work.
That can make a real difference on tall trees and on days with many ascents. Compare other ascent and descent gear if you prefer a mechanical rope-walking or foot ascender setup.

Powered ascenders have changed how some crews approach tall trees, especially where climbers make many ascents in a day. They do not replace good technique, but they leave more energy for the work itself.
This version comes without a battery or charger; confirm the exact batteries and charger it requires before you buy. Plan capacity for the number and height of ascents in a day.

A powered ascender must be used as the manufacturer directs, with a properly anchored rope and the required backup. Get training from a qualified instructor before using one. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Does it come with a battery?
faq.a: No. This listing is the tool only. Check the listing for the compatible battery and charger.

faq.q: Can I descend with it?
faq.a: Check the manufacturer's instructions for what the device is rated to do and always use a proper descent device and backup as directed.

name: Petzl William Carabiner (Auto-Locking)
title: Petzl William Carabiner: Large Auto-Locking Pear
meta: The Petzl William carabiner is a large pear-shaped aluminum connector with room for hitches and several eyes. Where it fits and how to inspect it.
tagline: A large pear-shaped aluminum carabiner for hitches and multiple attachments.
summary: The Petzl William carabiner is a large pear-shaped (HMS) aluminum connector, and the auto-locking version locks itself every time the gate closes. Its wide shape makes room for a friction hitch, rope eyes, and several attachments at once, which is why so many arborists use it at the bridge or hitch.
highlights: Room for hitches and several eyes

p: A friction hitch, a rope eye, and a pulley all need space on one carabiner, and a small D will crowd them. The William's large pear shape gives everything room to sit without binding, and the wide gate opening makes it easy to clip a rope eye or a bridge with gloves on.
The auto-locking gate closes and locks every time, so you are not relying on remembering to spin a sleeve. Compare other auto-locking carabiners if you want a smaller or steel option.
The William is also a common choice for connecting a rope bridge or for clipping a pulley and hitch together at the top of a hitch-climber setup.

Load the carabiner along its major axis, avoid three-way and cross loading, and keep the gate away from edges and tree contact where bark can push it open. Check that the lock engages fully after each clip.

Before every climb, inspect for cracks, sharp edges, wear grooves, and a gate that does not snap shut and lock. Retire it after a significant drop onto a hard surface. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Which locking version should I choose?
faq.a: Petzl offers the William in several gate styles. Auto-locking versions lock themselves, which many climbers prefer for life-support connections.

faq.q: Is aluminum strong enough for climbing?
faq.a: Yes, when the carabiner is rated for the use and loaded correctly. Check the strength markings on the spine.

name: Courant Top Koala Harness
title: Courant Top Koala Chest Harness for Koala Saddle
meta: The Courant Top Koala is a chest harness that adds shoulder support to the Courant Koala saddle. How it helps on SRS ascents and how to inspect it.
tagline: A chest harness that adds shoulder support to the Courant Koala saddle.
summary: The Courant Top Koala is a chest harness designed to pair with the Courant Koala saddle, adding shoulder support and a place to attach chest-mounted gear. Climbers running SRS often add a chest harness to keep upright on long ascents and to hold a chest ascender in position.
highlights: Chest harness for the Courant Koala saddle
Helps keep you upright on ascents
Spreads gear load across the shoulders

p: On a long SRS ascent, a chest harness keeps your upper body close to the rope and holds a chest ascender in the right position, so each stroke moves you up efficiently. It also helps carry the weight of gear hung from the saddle by sharing it with your shoulders.
The Top Koala is built to work with the Koala saddle so the attachment points line up properly. Compare other saddle parts and shoulder harnesses if you climb in a different saddle.

A chest harness also gives you a place to clip tools and keeps gear from pulling the back of the saddle down, which many climbers notice on long days. It can make a frog-style or rope-walking ascent feel noticeably smoother.
Adjust the straps so the harness sits snug without restricting your breathing or arm movement, and follow Courant's instructions for how it connects to the saddle.

A chest harness used to position ascent gear is part of your climbing system. Inspect webbing, stitching, and buckles before every climb. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Will the Top Koala fit other saddles?
faq.a: It is designed for the Courant Koala. Check the maker's compatibility information before using it with another saddle.

faq.q: Do I need a chest harness for SRS?
faq.a: Not always, but many climbers find it makes rope-walking and frog-style ascents more efficient.

name: Phoenix 3/4 in Hand Pruner
title: Phoenix Hand Pruner, 3/4 in Cut Capacity
meta: The Phoenix hand pruner makes clean cuts on twigs and small branches up to about 3/4 in. Where it fits in a pruning kit and how to keep it sharp.
tagline: A hand pruner for clean cuts on twigs and small branches up to about 3/4 in.
summary: The Phoenix hand pruner is a pair of pruning shears for clean cuts on twigs, suckers, and small branches up to about 3/4 in. It is the tool you reach for on detail work, where a saw is too much and a clean cut matters.
highlights: Good for detail and structural pruning
Fits in a holster on a belt or saddle

p: A good pair of hand pruners handles the small cuts that come up all day: suckers, water sprouts, deadwood twigs, and small branches on young trees. Making those cuts cleanly at the right point helps the tree seal the wound and leaves a tidy finish.
A 3/4 in capacity covers most small pruning work; step up to loppers or a hand saw for anything larger. Browse other pruners and loppers for bigger cuts.

Many climbers carry a hand pruner in a holster on the saddle for the small cuts that come up while moving through the crown. It is also a staple for ground workers cleaning up young trees, removing suckers, and finishing small cuts after the climber is done. A sharp, well-adjusted pruner leaves a cleaner wound than a saw on wood this size.
Keep the blade sharp and the pivot adjusted so the pruner cuts cleanly without crushing. Wipe sap off after use and oil the pivot to keep it moving freely and to prevent rust.
Do not twist the pruner or force it through wood larger than its capacity, which can spring the blades. Carry it in a holster and wear gloves. Follow ANSI A300 pruning practice.

faq.q: Can it cut larger than 3/4 in?
faq.a: Forcing larger cuts can damage the blades and leave ragged wounds. Use a lopper or hand saw for anything bigger.

faq.q: Bypass or anvil?
faq.a: Bypass pruners give the cleanest cuts on live wood. Check the listing for this pruner's blade style.

name: Husqvarna Recoil Starter Handle for 372XP
title: Husqvarna 372XP Starter Handle (Recoil Grip)
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 372XP starter handle for the recoil starter rope. When the grip needs replacing, how to fit it to the rope, and starter care tips.
tagline: A replacement recoil starter handle for the Husqvarna 372XP chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP starter handle replaces a cracked or broken grip on the saw's recoil starter rope. It is a small part, but a broken handle makes the saw awkward and unsafe to start.
highlights: Quick to fit when the starter rope is changed
Cheap spare to keep with your saw kit

p: The starter handle takes a hard pull every time you start the saw and gets knocked against the bar, the truck bed, and the ground. Once it cracks, it can cut your hand or break in the middle of a pull.
Replacing the handle is a quick job, often done at the same time as a new starter rope. Browse other power equipment parts for starter ropes and other wear items.

Recoil starter parts are among the most common wear items on a busy saw, so it makes sense to keep a spare handle and a length of starter rope with your saw kit. If the old handle broke because the rope was fraying or the starter was binding, fix that too, or the new handle will not last.
Thread the starter rope through the handle and tie it off as the service manual shows, so the knot sits inside the grip and the rope retracts fully. Check the rope for fraying while you are in there.

Start the saw on the ground with the chain brake on and a firm grip, never by drop-starting. Wear chainsaw protection, eye and hearing protection, and follow the operator's manual and ANSI Z133 when running or servicing a saw.

faq.q: Does it come with a starter rope?
faq.a: Check the listing. Handles are often sold alone, so you may need rope separately.

faq.q: Will it fit other Husqvarna saws?
faq.a: It is listed for the 372XP. Check your saw's parts list before using it on another model.

name: CMI 1/2 in Aluminum Rigging Block with 1/2 x 5 Sling
title: CMI Aluminum Rigging Block, 1/2 in, with 1/2 x 5 Sling
h1: CMI Aluminum Rigging Block, 1/2 in, with 1/2 x 5 Sling
meta: A CMI aluminum rigging block for 1/2 in rope paired with a 1/2 x 5 sling, ready to hang at a rigging point. How the kit works, rope sizing, and inspection tips.
tagline: A CMI aluminum rigging block for 1/2 in rope, paired with a matching sling.
summary: This CMI aluminum rigging block takes 1/2 in rope and comes paired with a 1/2 x 5 sling, so you have a ready-to-hang rigging point for pruning-size wood and smaller removals. Aluminum keeps the block light enough to carry up on your saddle.
highlights: Light enough to carry on the saddle
Good for light to medium rigging
specs: See markings on block and sling

body.h: A light rigging point you can carry up
p: For pruning cuts over a roof or small removals, you do not need a heavy steel block. An aluminum block sized for 1/2 in rope is light enough to carry on your saddle and strong enough for light to medium rigging. Hang it from the sling at the rigging point and run your lowering line through it.
Buying the block and sling together means they are sized to work as a pair. Compare other rigging kits if you rig heavier wood.
Kits like this also suit a climber who wants a personal rigging setup for small jobs without borrowing the crew's heavier gear.

Stay within the rated strength of the block, the sling, and the rope, and remember that rigging loads are dynamic: a short drop can multiply the force on the rigging point. Use a lowering device on the ground to control the load.

Before each job, check the side plates, sheave, and axle for cracks, grooves, and wobble, and look over the sling for cuts and abrasion. Rig only within the rated strength of every component, inspect gear before each job, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: Can I run 5/8 in rope through this block?
faq.a: No. It is sized for 1/2 in rope. Running oversized rope damages the rope and the block.

faq.q: Is aluminum strong enough for rigging?
faq.a: For loads within its rating, yes. For heavy removals choose a larger block rated for the loads you expect.

name: Samson 5/8 Arbor-Plex Rigging Rope
title: Samson Arbor-Plex 5/8 Rigging Rope: Buying Guide
meta: Samson Arbor-Plex 5/8 is a 12-strand rigging rope that splices easily and handles well for lowering wood on removals. Who it suits and how to inspect it.
tagline: A 5/8 in, 12-strand single braid rigging rope that is easy to splice and handle.
summary: Samson Arbor-Plex 5/8 is a 12-strand single braid rigging rope that is easy to splice and handle on the ground, making it a common choice for lowering wood on removals. The 5/8 in size sits between light pruning rigging and the heaviest rigging work.
highlights: A workhorse for medium to heavy rigging

p: A rigging rope takes abuse: it runs through blocks and lowering devices, drags through brush, and gets loaded hard again and again. Arbor-Plex's 12-strand single braid construction is simple to inspect and quick to splice an eye into, which crews value when they make their own slings and rigging lines.

At 5/8 in it handles medium to heavy rigging for most crews. Compare other rigging ropes if you want a lighter or heavier line. The typical price shown is for a 150 ft length; price varies with length.
Arbor-Plex is also offered in 1/2 in and 3/4 in, so crews often carry more than one size: a lighter line for pruning cuts and a heavier one for big wood.
Keep the rope away from saws, fuel, and chipper feed, and store it dry and out of the sun. Rotate ends so wear is spread along the length.

Inspect for cut or pulled strands, glazing from hot lowering, stiff spots, and core damage. Retire rope that has been shock loaded beyond its rating or shows damage. Rig only within the rated strength of every component, inspect gear before each job, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: Can I splice Arbor-Plex myself?
faq.a: Yes, 12-strand rope is among the easier ropes to splice. Learn from a qualified person and follow Samson's splicing instructions.

faq.q: Is Arbor-Plex suitable for climbing?
faq.a: No. Use it for rigging only and climb on rope that is made and rated for climbing.

name: Saddle Storage Bag
title: Saddle Storage Bag for Arborist Climbing Gear
meta: A saddle storage bag protects your climbing saddle from fuel, sun, and grit in the truck. What to look for, how to pack it, and why it helps gear last.
tagline: A bag that keeps your climbing saddle clean, dry, and away from fuel in the truck.
summary: A saddle storage bag gives your climbing saddle its own space in the truck, away from bar oil, fuel, saws, and grit. Keeping the saddle clean and protected helps the webbing and hardware last longer and makes inspection easier.
highlights: Dedicated bag for a climbing saddle
Protects from fuel, oil, and UV
Makes setup at the tree quicker
specs: Storing and carrying a climbing saddle
Check bag dimensions against your saddle

body.h: Why store your saddle in its own bag
p: Your saddle is the core of your life-support system, and the back of a work truck is a rough place for it. Fuel and bar oil weaken textiles, sunlight degrades webbing, and loose saws and files can nick straps. A saddle storage bag keeps it separate from all of that.
It also keeps your lanyard, carabiners, and hitch cord in one place so you can gear up quickly at the base of the tree. Browse other gear storage options for ropes and hardware.

If your saddle has a bridge, side D-rings, and gear loops, look for a bag deep enough that you do not have to fold the saddle tightly. Sharp creases and pressure from hardware can wear webbing over time, so a roomy bag is kinder to the saddle.
Let a wet saddle dry fully before bagging it, and do not pack sharp tools in with it. Clean off sap and grit regularly so it does not grind into the webbing.

Good storage helps your gear last, but it is no substitute for inspection. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I store a wet saddle in the bag?
faq.a: Dry it first. Storing wet gear in a closed bag can lead to mildew and faster wear.

faq.q: Will my saddle fit?
faq.a: Check the bag's dimensions against your saddle, especially if it has a large bridge or extra gear loops.

name: The Splice Shop Soft Canopy Anchor
title: The Splice Shop Soft Canopy Anchor for SRS
h1: The Splice Shop Soft Canopy Anchor
meta: The Splice Shop soft canopy anchor gives SRS climbers a light rope anchor in the canopy. How it sets up, when to use it, and how to inspect it.
tagline: A light rope canopy anchor for single rope technique climbers.
summary: The Splice Shop soft canopy anchor is a rope-based anchor for SRS climbers who want a light, packable way to set a canopy tie-in. Being soft, it protects the bark and weighs much less than a hardware-heavy setup.
highlights: Gentler on bark than hard hardware

body.h: How a soft canopy anchor is used
p: In SRS, your rope is fixed at an anchor rather than running over a branch and back to you. A soft canopy anchor wraps the tie-in limb and gives your rope a defined, protected attachment point, which reduces friction wear on the bark and keeps the rope from sawing into the union.
It is a light option for climbers who want to keep their kit simple. Compare other friction savers and anchors if you want a hardware-based setup.

Soft anchors pair well with a light SRS kit when you are moving between trees or working a large canopy. Because they are rope rather than metal, they also pack small and add little weight to the bag. Many climbers carry one alongside a hardware anchor so they can choose the right setup for each tree.

body.h: Choosing the anchor and inspecting it
p: Every SRS anchor depends on a sound tie-in point; assess the limb and union carefully before you commit, and follow the manufacturer's instructions for setup and any retrieval method.

Inspect the rope, splices, and any hardware for cuts, glazing, and wear before every climb. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I use it for MRS too?
faq.a: Check the maker's instructions for the configurations the anchor is designed for.

faq.q: How is a soft anchor retrieved?
faq.a: Retrieval depends on how it is set up. Follow the manufacturer's instructions and practice on the ground first.

name: Teufelberger Mule Bags
title: Teufelberger Mule Bags for Rope and Gear
meta: Teufelberger Mule bags carry rope and climbing gear to the job and keep it clean between climbs. What they hold, how they help on site, and care tips.
tagline: Durable Teufelberger bags for hauling rope and climbing gear to the job.
summary: Teufelberger Mule bags are carry bags for rope and climbing gear, built to take the knocks of a working tree crew. They keep your kit together, clean, and away from fuel and saws between climbs.
highlights: Gear and rope bags from Teufelberger
Shields rope from fuel, oil, and grit
Easy to carry from truck to tree

p: Rope is expensive and easy to damage. Bar oil, fuel, and chips do it no favors, and rope that is dragged across a gravel driveway picks up grit that wears it from the inside. A dedicated bag keeps it clean and makes it easy to carry rope and hardware to the base of the tree in one trip.
Mule bags are aimed at crews who move gear every day. Compare other gear bags for different sizes.

Bags like this also help the ground crew keep track of gear during a busy day, since each climber's kit stays together instead of spreading across the tailgate. It is a simple way to cut down on lost hardware and rope left in the brush.
Flake rope into the bag rather than coiling it, so it feeds out without kinks. Keep sharp tools out, dry wet gear before storing it, and empty the bag of debris regularly.

Storage keeps gear in good shape, but life-support equipment still needs inspection before every climb. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

faq.q: How much rope fits in a Mule bag?
faq.a: Capacity depends on the bag size and the rope diameter. Check the listing for the size you are ordering.

faq.q: Can I wash the bag?
faq.a: Brush it out and wash with mild soap and water, then air dry. Avoid solvents.
